summary: Creates the multidisciplinary team and product practices needed to discover, design, build, test, release and continuously improve student-facing digital capabilities.
detailSummary:
The Digital Innovation and Product Development Capability will establish a sustained multidisciplinary team around the continued evolution of the Student Experience Hub. The team will combine software engineering, product and experience design, user research and agile delivery, drawing on specialist architecture, data, integration, security, accessibility, change and service-management expertise through clear working interfaces.

The deliverable focuses on who delivers and how they work. It will establish one transparent product pipeline, disciplined discovery and prioritisation, continuous student and staff involvement, proportionate prototyping, engineering and quality practices, embedded assurance, controlled release, evaluation and a clear route into supported operation or clean closure.

The Student Experience Hub product, app architecture, platform foundations and operating costs are owned through 4.1.2. The team established here works within those foundations and can support the King’s Edge product demand under 4.1.4 before scaling across the wider app roadmap.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s does not currently have a sufficiently dependable multidisciplinary team or consistent product practices for turning emerging student-experience needs into working and sustainable digital capabilities.

Requirements are often addressed through conventional system change, local initiatives, temporary projects or standalone products. Demand can be difficult to prioritise, users may be involved too late, and promising prototypes can struggle to move through quality, assurance, release and support. Similar needs may be addressed several times without building institutional delivery capability.

This limits King’s ability to respond rapidly while maintaining quality and creates repeated dependence on temporary projects, separate procurements or unsupported local solutions.
caseForChange.opportunity:
A sustained multidisciplinary team with clear product practices can give King’s a faster and more disciplined route from need to supported change.

One transparent pipeline can connect prioritisation, discovery, service design, user research, prototyping, engineering, quality, assurance, release and evaluation. Students and service owners can shape decisions while solutions remain adaptable, and specialist Digital and IT functions can be involved throughout rather than acting only as late-stage gates.

A clear harden-or-close model allows experimentation without creating unmanaged legacy. The same team and practices can first serve King’s Edge and then support a growing portfolio of journeys through the shared app and platform owned by 4.1.2.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge is generating an immediate pipeline of substantial product requirements while the Student Experience Hub and its app and platform foundations are being established.

Those foundations will not create a more responsive institution on their own. King’s also needs the people, decision rights, methods and capacity to turn needs into tested and supported product change. Without a shared team and operating model, early demand is likely to be channelled into disconnected delivery routes even if the target architecture is coherent.

Establishing the capability now allows the first Edge-led work to prove both the team model and the product lifecycle before demand expands across the wider student app.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
King’s has an enduring multidisciplinary digital product team with a transparent pipeline, clear decision rights and repeatable practices for discovery, user research, design, engineering, quality, assurance, release and continuous improvement.

Emerging needs are explored with students and service owners before substantial commitment. Work moves predictably from evidence and prototype into controlled live use, supported operation or clean closure. Team capacity and product priorities are governed coherently, and live-service evidence directly informs what the team does next.

The team can support several product demands while working within the app and platform foundations owned through 4.1.2. Digital innovation becomes faster and more sustainable because the institution retains both the capability and the learning generated through delivery.

benefits.title: King’s responds more quickly to emerging student needs
benefits.statement: Priority needs can be translated into tested digital responses in shorter cycles, with student and staff evidence shaping development before large commitments are made.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From establishment of the first delivery pipeline
benefits.successLooksLike: Priority needs move predictably from discovery to evaluated live use, and users can influence solutions while they remain adaptable.

benefits.title: Digital delivery becomes more predictable and evidence-led
benefits.statement: A transparent pipeline, consistent product practices and embedded quality and assurance make priorities, progress, trade-offs and release decisions clearer.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.realisationPeriod: As the operating model becomes routine
benefits.successLooksLike: Demand is prioritised through one route, delivery cycles use consistent evidence and standards, and capacity and release decisions can be explained and reviewed.

benefits.title: Successful innovation becomes sustainable institutional provision
benefits.statement: Valuable changes have a defined route into secure, supported and appropriately owned operation, while the team and its professional capability remain available for continuous improvement.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the first harden-or-close cycle, increasing as the team becomes recurrent
benefits.successLooksLike: Successful capabilities have explicit ownership and support arrangements, unsuccessful trials close cleanly, and the multidisciplinary team has an approved route into business as usual.

steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: Recruit, appoint or assign the core multidisciplinary team from September through November 2026. Establish its leadership, decision rights, role coverage, interfaces with product owners and specialist Digital and IT functions, initial demand pipeline and capacity plan, with the team ready for full delivery from December 2026.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish how the team turns demand into delivered and supported product change. Put in place a transparent intake and prioritisation route, discovery and user-research practices, service design and prototyping methods, engineering and quality expectations, definitions of ready and done, embedded assurance workflows, release and documentation disciplines, and regular planning, review and retrospective routines.

steps.title: Prove the end-to-end product lifecycle through King’s Edge
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, use the King’s Edge roadmap to run repeated end-to-end product cycles. Move needs through discovery, design, prototyping, development, quality and assurance, controlled release and evaluation, then either harden successful changes for continued service or conclude them cleanly. Use the evidence to refine team roles, practices and handoffs.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make the team’s operating practices routine. Establish reliable pipeline and capacity planning, a predictable discovery and release rhythm, regular quality and assurance activity, effective collaboration on incidents and maintenance, clear ownership and handover arrangements, and evidence-led review of product performance and benefits.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices across the wider app roadmap
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, apply the established operating model across a growing portfolio of student journeys. Increase throughput and support concurrent work while preserving continuous user involvement, disciplined prioritisation, quality, embedded assurance, learning and sustainable ownership. Use evidence to refine the team shape, professional practices and balance between new delivery and live-service work.

steps.title: Embed an enduring institutional product-development capability
steps.summary: From November 2028 to June 2029, establish the multidisciplinary team, its recurrent staffing, professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with product owners and specialist Digital and IT services as an enduring institutional capability. Ensure the team can respond to new priorities and continuously improve live products without reverting to disconnected local builds, separate procurements or unsupported prototypes.
